true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overrides the existing width/height API

Ruby does not support method overloading. The new self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces the self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate width and height values will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking thumbnail/avatar downsizing paths that use the original signature.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured image and attachment limits

Replacing Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 MB breaks sites whose configured limits differ: attachments or images allowed above 10 MB by an administrator are rejected client-side, while files above a lower configured limit pass client validation and fail later on the server. The hardcoded value in the 413 handler at line 246 likewise reports 10 MB even when the server limit that produced the rejection is different.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Animated GIF detection fails for extensionless upload tempfiles

Upload and downloaded-file tempfiles normally have paths without a .gif extension. OptimizedImage.optimize selects its animated instructions only when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, so passing tempfile.path here never selects that path despite allow_animation being supplied. The normal downsize instructions use `#{from}[0]`, selecting only the first frame, so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened instead of being resized as an animation. The extensionless destination can also prevent ImageMagick from inferring the intended output format.

Failed image conversions are retried blindly and then ignored

The loop ignores the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails—for example for an unsupported/corrupt image or an SVG matched by FileHelper.is_image?—it invokes the same failing conversion up to five times and then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file. This wastes external-process work and makes the automatic-downsizing feature fail opaquely instead of falling back or reporting the conversion failure.

URL download limit is changed to a fixed 10 MB for every upload type

The API URL-download cap no longer uses SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and is fixed at 10 megabytes regardless of whether the upload is an image or an attachment. This rejects remotely fetched files that the site configuration would allow above 10 MB, and it downloads non-image attachments up to 10 MB even when the applicable configured limit is lower; those attachments cannot be downsized and are only rejected after the transfer.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes when host is nil

The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! without checking for nil. Creating an EmbeddableHost with a missing/blank host (e.g. a direct API POST with no host param reaching the model, or EmbeddableHost.new.valid?) raises NoMethodError instead of failing the format validation and returning a validation error, producing a 500 rather than render_json_error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

Update/destroy raise NoMethodError for unknown ids instead of returning 404

update and destroy look up the host with where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host)/host.destroy on the result. For a stale or invalid id the lookup returns nil, so save_host dereferences nil.host= and destroy calls nil.destroy, returning a 500. save_host also dereferences params[:embeddable_host] on line 23 without checking presence, so malformed requests crash the same way.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim and can break host matching or the migration

Hosts from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into INSERT SQL without normalization or quoting. Values stored as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (forms the old setting and specs explicitly allowed) are inserted with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host (a bare hostname), so migrated sites silently lose embedding permission for those hosts. true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or unmatched

The migration unconditionally calls [0]['id'] on the result of joining categories to the embed_category site setting. On installs that never set embed_category, or whose stored value is not exactly a category name, the query returns no rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking deployment/upgrades. The fallback on line 15 has the same unsafe [0]['value'] pattern.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Edit action crashes for hosts whose category cannot be resolved

The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') unconditionally. A host whose category_id points at a deleted category, the uncategorized sentinel, or a category not present in the client's category list hydrates with category undefined/null (store._lookupSubType returns Discourse.Category.findById(id), which can be undefined), so clicking the pencil throws a TypeError and the row can never be edited or fixed in the UI.

No uniqueness constraint allows ambiguous duplicate hosts

Neither the model nor the migration adds a uniqueness validation/index on host. Admins can create two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then returns whichever row the database happens to return first, so embedded topics from that host are filed into an unpredictable category and host_allowed?/category selection becomes nondeterministic.

Plural _id hydration discards ids and fabricates undefined entries when the collection is not sideloaded

For any *_ids key, the new code maps ids through _lookupSubType, assigns the result (which may be an array of undefined when root does not contain the sideloaded collection), and deletes the original *_ids key. Unlike the singular branch, which only replaces the key when a record is found, the plural branch loses the id data and leaves an array of undefined objects for any payload that carries ids without embedding the records, a regression affecting all RestModel types, not just fruits/embeddable hosts.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row

TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when the user is receiving notifications through a watched category or has never visited/interacted with the topic in a way that created a topic_users row. Lines 107-113 then call tu.notification_level and tu.save! unconditionally, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. The action should create/update the row (e.g. via TopicUser.change, as set_notifications does) rather than assuming one exists.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
No tests cover the new unsubscribe endpoint or that the topic URL reaches the email

The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the fixture builder but adds no expectation that the unsubscribe_url appears in the body/HTML, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all. The watching/tracking -> regular and regular/muted -> muted transitions, the missing-TopicUser case, the slug-redirect case, and unauthenticated/inaccessible-topic behavior are all untested, so the nil-row crash and level-transition regressions above would pass CI undetected.

Per-topic unsubscribe mutates notification state on a GET request The new routes in config/routes.rb expose unsubscribe as GET and this action immediately changes and saves notification_level. Any logged-in browser request to the emailed URL therefore mutates state without confirmation or CSRF protection, so mail-scanner link prefetching, browser prefetch, or a cross-site /link to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe can silently mute/downgrade a topic the user never intended to unsubscribe from. A state change like this should require POST (or an explicit confirmation step) with CSRF protection.

Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and live updates

Unlike TopicsController#set_notifications, which uses TopicUser.change, this action assigns tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! directly. That bypasses the notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id (user_changed) bookkeeping and the MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change publish (and after-save observers) performed by TopicUser.change, so other open clients and topic-tracking state keep showing the old watching/tracking level until a full reload, and the change is not recorded as a user-initiated notification change.

unsubscribe_link translation now hard-requires unsubscribe_url for every unsubscribe email

config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to include %{unsubscribe_url}, and both the HTML path here and body (line 90) render it via I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. template_args only contains unsubscribe_url when the caller passes it, and MessageBuilder treats it as optional (only UserNotifications#send_notification_email supplies it). Any other current/future/test caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without a topic-specific URL will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send; the new spec change that had to add unsubscribe_url to an existing generic builder illustrates the coupling. The per-topic line should be conditional or the translation should be given a safe default.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation has a write side effect and double-counts a single signup attempt

EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and writes last_match_at. Validations run repeatedly for one logical attempt: UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save (which validates again), so one blocked signup is counted at least twice, and any other code that merely checks user.valid? (tests, console, unrelated flows) also falsely records a match. The statistics update should happen once per actual blocked attempt, not inside a reusable EachValidator.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the supplied address with an exact `where(email: email)` match, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator normalizes case or surrounding whitespace before lookup/storage. A blocked address such as bad@spam.example can therefore be resubmitted as Bad@Spam.Example and will not match, bypassing the block even though mail delivery treats the domain case-insensitively. Normalize (at minimum downcase/strip) both when creating BlockedEmail records and when checking them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
rejectedEmails array is shared mutable prototype state

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` declares one array on the controller prototype, so pushObject in createAccount mutates state shared by every instance of CreateAccountController rather than per-instance state. Rejected addresses can leak between controller instances (notably tests and any non-singleton use) and are never reset. Initialize the array per instance (e.g. in init) and clear it when the modal/account flow is reset.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content element

poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every item. Ordinary RSS items commonly have description instead of content (and Atom/RSS variants expose different fields), so i.content can be nil and this raises NoMethodError. Because the exception is inside rss.items.each with sidekiq retry disabled, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll and prevents all remaining items from being imported.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent imports for the same URL race the unique embed_url index

import does a non-atomic check-then-create: it looks up TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed after PostCreator runs. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic/PollFeed executions for the same new URL can both see no embed, both create topics/posts, and then the second TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the unique index instead of returning the already-created post, failing the job after doing duplicate creation work. The lookup/create needs an atomic rescue/retry or locking strategy.

Disqus import drops the category option and now depends on fetching the live source site

The import task removed the --category option and replaced local topic creation (with the thread's title, permalink body, created_at, and chosen category) with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs open(url).read on each Disqus thread link. Existing invocations using -c will no longer place topics in the requested category, threads whose original site is offline, moved, or blocks fetching will fail the import, and the thread's original creation date is no longer used for the imported topic.

Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job

The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new/retrieve, but EmbedController#best never instantiates TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). The mock expectation will not be satisfied and this spec fails, leaving the actual enqueue arguments (user_id and embed_url) untested. The spec should expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic instead.

Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization

TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for such posts. Neither import nor absolutize_urls strips script tags, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs, or other dangerous markup, and PollFeed passes RSS/Atom content directly into import. A malicious or compromised feed item can therefore store arbitrary HTML/JavaScript as post.cooked, which is rendered raw in Discourse and in embed views, giving stored XSS in forum visitors' browsers.

absolutize_urls only fixes root-relative URLs, leaving other relative links broken

absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Feed and readability content frequently uses document-relative URLs such as href="page2.html" or src="images/pic.jpg" and protocol-relative URLs such as src="//cdn.example.com/x.jpg"; those are left untouched, so after import they resolve against the Discourse host instead of the source site and produce wrong links or 404 images in the imported post.

import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with no timeout or size limit

TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, redirect restriction, or response-size cap before Readability parsing. Via EmbedController/RetrieveTopic the URL is user-influenced (constrained only by host equality at the retriever layer), so requests can make the server fetch large or slow resources on the embeddable host, exhausting job workers/memory; the fetched result is then published as a topic, which can also disclose content the server can reach but an anonymous visitor could not. Add timeouts, size limits, and scheme/host validation inside import_remote itself.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() emits an invalid -ms- property and does not translate values for legacy syntax

The mixin emits '-ms-align-items', which is not a recognized property; IE10's legacy property is -ms-flex-align. It also passes the standard value verbatim to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, whose legacy value grammars use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end. Current call sites use center/baseline, which happen to coincide, but the new shared mixin silently produces invalid declarations for flex-start/flex-end and provides no IE10 alignment despite claiming legacy flexbox support.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin maps flex order incorrectly for 2009 flexbox syntax

The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the standard order property, but box-ordinal-group is 1-based (the default is 1) while flex order is 0-based (the default is 0). For equivalence, the legacy properties must be $val + 1. As written, order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel behave as orders 1 and 2 in old WebKit/Firefox, and any future order(0) would be invalid/ignored there, so legacy browsers can order header elements differently from modern browsers.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

false_positives.candidate:
Flex header children cannot shrink, so a long topic title can push the panel out of the header

Making .d-header .contents a flex container turns .title, .extra-info-wrapper, and .panel into flex items, which default to min-width:auto and therefore cannot shrink below their content size. .extra-info-wrapper (given order(2) in topic.scss) contains the current topic title/category badges and has no flex, min-width:0, or overflow constraint added in this change. A long title will consequently force .panel (order(3), margin-left:auto) to overflow/clip at the right edge of the header instead of the title area truncating as it could under the previous float layout.

Small-action button loses its right alignment inside the new flex container

.small-action is now display:flex via flexbox() at line 264, making its direct children flex items. The button rule inside it still relies on 'float: right' (line 309), but floats have no effect on flex items per the flexbox spec. With no margin-left:auto on the button or justify-content on the container, the button will now sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the far right of the row, changing the layout of small-action posts (e.g. close/split notices).

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional inclusion method is missing the required question mark

The method is defined as `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. Other inclusion predicates in this serializer use the `?` form, and ActiveModelSerializers only invokes `include_<attribute>?` to decide whether to emit an attribute. As a result this guard is never called, so `website_name` is emitted (as null) even when `website` is blank, instead of being omitted from the JSON.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalid website URIs can raise during serialization after the rescued parse

Only the first `URI(website.to_s).host` call on line 138 is protected by the modifier `rescue nil`. The subsequent `URI(website.to_s).path` calls on lines 143, 146 and 149 are unprotected, so a stored website that parses to a host but raises `URI::InvalidURIError` on re-parsing (for example containing spaces or invalid characters in the path) will raise out of `website_name` and break serialization of the whole user profile instead of falling back to the host name.

New website_name branches and edge cases are untested

The new specs cover only unrelated domains, exact host match, and website-as-parent. They do not cover the sibling-subdomain branch added at serializer lines 144-146, a website subdomain of the instance host, a website without a scheme or with invalid URI characters, a blank website (verifying the attribute is omitted), or the TL0-anonymous restriction. Regressions in those branches, including serialization errors and information leakage, would pass this suite.

Same-domain detection is inconsistent for website subdomains of the instance domain

If the website is a subdomain of the instance domain (website `blog.example.com`, instance `example.com`), the first branch fails, the equal-label-count branch fails, and `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)` is also false, so only the host is shown. The reverse parent case and the sibling case (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, line 146) do show the full path, so equally same-registrable-domain URLs are treated inconsistently and the feature silently does not apply to subdomain websites.

website_name bypasses the untrusted-user restriction applied to website

`website_name` is added to the general attributes list but not to the `untrusted_attributes` list at lines 105-111, which hides `website`, `location`, bios, etc. from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Anonymous viewers therefore still receive the website host, and the full path when it matches the instance domain, even though the underlying `website` attribute is deliberately withheld from them.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb

The spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (the companion success example on line 125 correctly uses :delete). Controller specs dispatch by action name rather than through the router, so this test passes even though the verb it documents does not exist; it would not catch a routing/verb mismatch and misdocuments the API contract. It should use :delete like the success case.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size

totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this reports 2 pages instead of 1, and for 100/50 it reports 3 instead of 2. Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page and navigates to an empty phantom page. The formula should be a ceiling division (with the zero-count case handled separately).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Group creation silently discards the alias_level chosen in the UI

The client's Group#asJSON sends alias_level (along with name and visible) on POST /admin/groups, and the admin form renders the alias-level selector for new groups, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A group created with e.g. alias_level 'everyone' is therefore saved with the column default (0/nobody) with no error, and the admin must edit the group again to set the intended mentioning permissions.

Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset parameters

limit and offset are taken directly from params with only to_i coercion. A caller can pass limit=1000000 to force the server to load and serialize every member of a very large (e.g. automatic) group in a single request, defeating the new pagination and causing heavy memory/response load; negative values (limit=-1, offset=-5) are passed to ActiveRecord/Postgres and can raise a 500 error. Both values need clamping to a sane range (e.g. limit within 1..some maximum, offset >= 0).

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fallback list mixes String and Symbol locale identities

The list is built as [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq: locale and I18n.locale are not normalized to Symbol here, so a String locale such as "de" and the Symbol :de are treated as distinct entries by uniq, by @loaded_locales.include? in the accelerator, and by backend translation hashes. That can cause duplicate fallback attempts, repeated loading of the same YAML file under a different key type, and missed loaded-checks. Normalize every entry to a Symbol (and drop nil before uniq) before returning the chain.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests

Fallback locale files are loaded only from ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. The patched backend's translate path in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb still loads only config.locale, while this codebase explicitly loads locale YAML on demand. Mailers, background jobs, rake tasks, console, and any translation performed before this before_filter therefore look up the fallback locale in a backend that has never loaded its YAML file, so they return 'translation missing' instead of the site-default/English string. Loading must happen in the translation/fallback path itself, not only in the web controller.

Fallback lookup depends on database-backed SiteSetting on every miss

FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time I18n::Backend::Fallbacks handles a missing translation. SiteSetting is database/cache backed, so translation lookups made during boot, migrations, seed/rake tasks, or when the settings table/cache is not yet available can raise or fail instead of falling back, and hot missing-translation paths repeatedly pay a settings lookup. It also raises NoMethodError if default_locale is ever nil. Capture/derive the site default without a per-lookup database-backed call, handle nil, and refresh it when the setting changes.

Loading a fallback locale does not invalidate the translation LRU cache

ensure_loaded!/load_locale add translations for a newly loaded locale but never clear @cache. I18n.translate caches no-argument results (including a frozen 'translation missing' result produced before the fallback locale was loaded) keyed only by key, current locale, and backend. After ensure_loaded! later loads the fallback file, subsequent lookups can keep returning the cached missing/frozen string for the life of the process (until an unrelated reload!). Clear the cache when a locale is actually loaded.

No tests cover fallback ordering, loading, or pluralized fallbacks

This change replaces the global I18n.fallbacks object, moves pluralization setup, removes config.i18n.fallbacks from production/profile, and adds on-demand fallback loading, but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying user-locale -> site-default -> :en ordering, fallback of pluralized/interpolated keys (which bypass the accelerator cache), behaviour when the site default changes, or non-request contexts. Add backend-level specs for those cases before relying on this in production.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile

UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method inherited from UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 and no no-arg overload exists in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. This is a compilation failure. It should be called as isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Requiring a known user breaks initial discoverable-passkey login

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) now requires user != null, and authenticate() at line 115 and challenge(context,error,field) at line 137 use it to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context). On the initial login page no user is known yet, which is exactly the discoverable/resident-key passkey flow that identifies the user from the credential, so fillContextForm is never called, the conditional-UI challenge/autocomplete data is not rendered, and passwordless login from UsernamePasswordForm is broken. The same applies after a failed initial password attempt, where bad-password handling clears the user before challenge() re-renders the form. Previously fillContextForm was called when the user was not yet selected. The guard should be based on passkeys being enabled, not on a user already being present; the known-user check is only relevant to showing that user's authenticators.

false_positives.candidate:
Always hiding WebAuthn authenticators defeats the no-credential guard for known users

shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() now unconditionally returns false, so WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() never builds WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean and never takes its empty-authenticators early return at WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:104-107. Combined with UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() checking only the realm passkeys flag and user != null (not whether that user is configured for a passwordless credential), a re-authenticating user with no passkey credential will still be rendered the conditional-UI/WebAuthn form even though no credential can succeed. This contradicts the stated expectation in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey that users without a passkey should not see WebAuthn elements; that test only covers realm-level passkeys disabled, not the passkeys-enabled/user-without-credential case.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative queryset slicing raises AssertionError, despite the comment claiming Django handles it

The advanced-features branch does list(queryset[cursor.offset:stop]) with cursor.offset < 0, accompanied by the false claim that 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically.' Django QuerySet slicing explicitly raises AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported.' A crafted cursor such as 0:-1:0 supplied by an authorized admin therefore causes an unhandled 500. The same crash remains for negative offsets with is_prev cursors in the fallback branch at line 886 and in BasePaginator.get_result at line 184, which now clamps only non-prev cursors.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the endpoint's datetime ordering key

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime and this raises TypeError whenever build_cursor processes a non-empty page. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via strftime before scaling. The optimized_pagination=true path therefore returns a 500 instead of audit-log results for authorized users.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
New optimized pagination path is added without any tests

This PR adds a user-controlled optimized_pagination branch, a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, and changes slicing behavior in the shared BasePaginator, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for first/next/prev pages over datetime-ordered audit logs, crafted negative-offset cursors, or the superuser/global-access gating. Such tests would have caught that the new paginator crashes on datetime keys and on negative offsets before merge.

value_from_cursor does not convert cursor timestamps back to datetimes

value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged, unlike DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor which converts the millisecond timestamp to a timezone-aware datetime. BasePaginator.build_queryset then uses that raw numeric value as the bound in an extra() comparison against AuditLogEntry.datetime. Subsequent pages will compare/filter a datetime column against an integer timestamp, producing incorrect filtering or a database/type error, so even fixing get_item_key would not make multi-page optimized pagination return the correct rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset slicing raises instead of being handled by Django

The advanced-features branch passes cursor.offset (parsed from the user-supplied cursor string) directly as queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, claiming the Django ORM handles this. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') on negative slices, and the same applies to the is_prev branch in BasePaginator.get_result (line 182-184) which also leaves offset unclamped. Any admin hitting the audit-log endpoint with a crafted negative-offset cursor gets a 500, so the advertised feature does not work and adds a trivial error/DoS path.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset slicing raises instead of being handled by Django

The advanced-features branch passes cursor.offset (parsed from the user-supplied cursor string) directly as queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, claiming the Django ORM handles this. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') on negative slices, and the same applies to the is_prev branch in BasePaginator.get_result (line 182-184) which also leaves offset unclamped. Any admin hitting the audit-log endpoint with a crafted negative-offset cursor gets a 500, so the advertised feature does not work and adds a trivial error/DoS path.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering of its only caller

OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint calls this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on the datetime attribute and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does. build_cursor calls get_item_key on every non-empty page (TypeError on datetime) and build_queryset compares the datetime column against an int. The optimized_pagination=true path will therefore 500 or mis-filter for audit logs instead of paginating them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Flush-side max_segment_spans safeguard removed while insert cap is inconsistent

_load_segment_data no longer drops segments exceeding max_segment_spans (the metric and logger.error branch were removed), so the only remaining span-count protection is the Lua cap. That cap is hardcoded to 1000 while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans defaults to 1001 and is configurable, and it only runs on the insert path: segments created before this change, created while script loading fails, or grown by the Python-side ZADD pipeline before Lua runs can now be loaded and flushed unbounded (bounded only by the 10MiB byte cap), reintroducing the memory/segment-size risk the removed guard protected against, with no metric when eviction truncates a segment.

No test covers eviction, the sorted-set merge, or the reduced redirect depth

The test changes in this PR only add the new end_timestamp_precise argument to existing Span constructions. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment to verify ZPOPMIN eviction (which spans survive, whether the root/segment span can be evicted, and final flushed contents), no test with duplicate payloads across merged sets to verify score handling, and no test near the new 1000 redirect-depth limit. The core behavioral change of the PR is therefore unverified.

Redirect depth limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000

The redirect-following loop cap drops from 10000 to 1000 and the comment explaining that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly is deleted. Traces whose parent chain exceeds 1000 redirects will now stop following redirects early, so spans land in separate span-buf:s:* sets and are flushed as fragmented/incomplete segments rather than one segment. This is a correctness regression for deep traces unrelated to the 1000-span eviction cap (chain depth and span count are different dimensions).

Switching span buffers from sets to sorted sets breaks in-flight Redis data

The script and SpansBuffer now use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZADD/ZSCAN on span-buf:s:* keys, but segments already buffered before deployment are Redis SETs created with SADD. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for sorted-set commands on those keys, so process_spans/flush_segments will error for in-flight segments until their TTL expires (redis_ttl defaults to 3600s), losing or stalling those spans. No migration, type check, or dual-read handling is included.

Unrelated audit-log pagination feature is bundled into the spans change

This PR is titled and described as a spans-buffer optimization, but it also adds a new user-controlled 'optimized_pagination' mode to the organization audit-log endpoint, gated on is_superuser/has_global_access and backed by the new OptimizedCursorPaginator. This changes behavior of a sensitive audit-log API (whose paginator is broken for datetime keys and crashes on negative offsets, per the paginator findings) without any endpoint tests, changelog, or feature-flag rollout. It should be split out and reviewed/tested independently rather than shipped hidden inside the spans change.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM and corrupts duplicate span scores

Both zunionstore calls omit an AGGREGATE clause, so Redis defaults to SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets (e.g. a re-delivered span, or a span already zadded under the destination key by process_spans before the Lua merge), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values (roughly double, e.g. year 2077). Eviction via ZPOPMIN then orders by corrupted scores, so duplicated spans are effectively never evicted and eviction order no longer reflects end time. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) explicitly.

process_batch now hard-requires end_timestamp_precise and will crash the batch if absent

Span previously did not need end_timestamp_precise; the existing consumer test payload omitted it and had to be modified in this PR to add it. Using val['end_timestamp_precise'] raises KeyError for any ingest-spans message lacking the field, failing the entire batch in process_batch (and, under Arroyo, causing redelivery/retry of the same poison batch) instead of defaulting the score (e.g. val.get('end_timestamp_precise', 0) or the message timestamp). Either tolerate a missing value or prove from the schema that it is mandatory and add a test for the missing-field case.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60s with a dead invalidation function and a hash()-based key

Eligibility is stored under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}` for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) is never called anywhere and no option-change hook invokes it, so removing a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` keeps inflating its counts (and adding one delays correct counts) until expiry. The key also relies on Python's built-in `hash()` of the project tuple rather than a stable, collision-resistant encoding of the project IDs (e.g. joining the sorted IDs), so distinct project sets can collide/share an eligibility decision within a process.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility uses closure `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` actually queried

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` (which `get_event_stats_factory` changes for dashboard discover-split widgets, e.g. passing `discover` or the original scoped dataset), but the eligibility check passes the outer closure variable `dataset`. When the two differ, counts are transformed for a dataset that is not being queried (e.g. upsampling a transactions/discover query, where `sample_weight` is invalid/zero) or not transformed for the errors query that is actually run, producing wrong counts or Snuba errors for split dashboard widgets.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental gitlink/submodule added to repository root

This adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing only `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, i.e. an accidental nested-repository gitlink unrelated to error upsampling. Merging it creates a bogus submodule entry at the repo root that can break checkouts/tooling expecting it to be a normal path and pollutes the tree; it should be removed from the PR.

Error-focus check reads request.GET instead of the query actually being executed

`_is_error_focused_query` only inspects `request.GET['query']`, ignoring the `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`. That argument is rewritten by callers (dashboard split builds `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction` and `({query}) AND event.type:transaction`, and event-stats can execute multiple/derived queries). Consequently a transaction-only subquery can be upsampled because the original request mentioned errors, while an error-only subquery whose request parameter is empty or formatted differently is not upsampled, yielding incorrect `sum(sample_weight)` counts for transactions or missed upsampling for errors.

Internal upsampled_count function is exposed as a public query function

Unlike the neighbouring private internal function (which sets `private=True`), `upsampled_count` is registered without `private=True`, so any API user can send `upsampled_count()` directly as a y-axis/field on discover queries for arbitrary, non-allowlisted projects. That bypasses the all-projects-allowlisted and errors-only gating in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and returns misleading weighted counts (or errors on datasets without `sample_weight`); it should be marked private so only the server-side column transformation can invoke it.

upsampled_count sums sample_weight without coalescing missing weights to 1

The new aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`/`ifNull` handling. The transform in error_upsampling.py applies it to every `count()` for an allowlisted project, including events ingested before client error sampling existed or sent by SDKs that did not set a client sample rate, whose `sample_weight` can be NULL. In ClickHouse `sum` over NULLs yields NULL/0 rather than counting those events as weight 1, so historical/unsampled errors silently disappear from upsampled timeseries instead of being counted once.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error events can be paired with the wrong error IDs when nodestore results are missing

fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids but then zips error_ids with events.values() from nodestore.backend.get_multi. get_multi is keyed by node_id and may omit missing events, so if any event is absent the remaining values shift and are paired with the wrong event_id. This can attach the wrong title, message, and timestamp to an error in the Seer summary request, or drop/misattribute errors silently.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Table widget renders empty data when feature flag is enabled

When the organization has the use-table-widget-visualization feature, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData containing data: [] and empty meta, instead of converting result.data/result.meta and the widget fields into tabular data. Any dashboard table widget for such an organization will therefore show an empty table with no columns, losing the previously displayed query results.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mutual-exclusion validation for age/timestamp misses age=0

validate_timestamp and validate_age check self.initial_data.get('age')/get('timestamp') for truthiness. A report containing timestamp plus age=0 (a valid freshly-generated report age) will pass both validators even though the serializer intends to reject reports that mix the Working Draft timestamp field with the Editor's Draft age field, weakening the spec validation added in this change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Error timestamps are compared against replay segment timestamps in different units

gen_request_data compares error_events timestamps, which come from the stored event payload as epoch seconds, directly against replay segment event timestamps, which are rrweb timestamps in epoch milliseconds. Because milliseconds are roughly 1000x larger, all errors will be yielded before the first breadcrumb regardless of their actual chronological position, so the AI summary receives error context in the wrong order.

Hidden span attributes are only hidden while searching

The new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES list (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only in the branch taken when searchQuery is non-empty. When searchQuery is empty, sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns sortAttributes(attributes) unchanged, so the supposedly hidden internal attributes remain visible in the default attributes list and only disappear after the user types a search query.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive and does not trim whitespace

Codes are generated as lowercase hex and displayed/copyable as `XXXXX-XXXXX`, but verification only does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` with no toLowerCase() or trim(). A user who transcribes the code in uppercase (as the placeholder's uppercase X styling suggests) or with surrounding whitespace is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode even though they typed the correct code, effectively locking recovery users out. The same un-normalized comparison exists in the disable endpoint (disable.ts line 61); normalize (trim + lowercase) in both places.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Single-use backup code can be replayed by concurrent logins

Consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize() reads user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then updates the row nulling that entry. Two simultaneous login attempts with the same code can both read the pre-consumption value, both pass the check, and both write back an equivalent list, so the supposedly single-use code (promised as 'can be used exactly once' in the UI copy) authenticates more than once. Consumption needs an atomic/transactional compare-and-update or locking to guarantee one-time use.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code can be used without the account password

Password verification is skipped whenever any totpCode is present (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`), while the new branch at line 131 accepts a backupCode independently of totpCode. A direct credentials request supplying a valid backupCode plus any non-empty dummy totpCode therefore skips verifyPassword entirely and logs in with the backup code as a single factor. Backup codes are long-lived recovery secrets meant to replace only the TOTP factor, not the password, so anyone who obtains one code (e.g. a photographed/stored list) gains full account access without knowing the password.

Closing the modal on the backup-codes step desyncs 2FA state

On successful enable the handler now only advances to DisplayBackupCodes and defers onEnable() (which refreshes the parent page's 2FA state) and resetState() to the explicit Close button (lines 261-270). If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (X/Esc/backdrop via onOpenChange), the parent still shows 2FA as disabled even though the server enabled it, and the modal's step state remains DisplayBackupCodes, so reopening it lands on stale backup codes instead of the password step. onEnable/reset must also run on dialog close once enablement has succeeded.

First 2FA test never dismisses the new backup-codes step and backup login is untested

The 'enable 2FA and login using 2FA' test still proceeds straight from fillOtp to asserting the two-factor switch, but enabling now ends on the DisplayBackupCodes step and onEnable is only fired by the backup-codes Close button, so this test no longer drives the flow it asserts on. Only the second test was updated (download/copy/close), and the file itself notes at line 12 that login and disable with a backup code are untested. The new security-critical paths — successful backup-code login, rejection of a wrong code, and single-use invalidation of a consumed code — have no coverage, so regressions in them would ship undetected.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar

The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array (handleNewBooking can set it to null, and several other callers set it to []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws a TypeError, breaking EventManager.create for events using Google Meet location without a destination calendar. false_positives.candidate:
Any attendee can add arbitrary guests and modify the organizer's calendar event

Authorization succeeds if the caller's email merely matches any existing attendee (`isAttendee`). That grants a non-organizer guest write access to the booking: they can add unlimited arbitrary people, who are persisted as attendees, receive scheduled-event emails/ICS invites, and are pushed to the organizer's calendar via updateCalendarAttendees. The bookings UI only exposes this to the booking owner/team, so the API is substantially more permissive than the intended organizer/team-admin surface.

Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's

EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the booking (including `booking.user.credentials`/`destinationCalendar`) belongs to the organizer loaded from booking.userId. When a team admin/owner (or attendee) adds guests, the code tries to update the calendar event with the caller's credentials, so the organizer's calendar is not updated (or another user's calendar integration is used). It should load and use the booking organizer's user/credentials, as the booking owner is whose calendar holds the event.

Guest list has no size limit, enabling attendee/email spam

`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no .min(1)/.max() bound. A single authorized (including merely-attendee, per the handler) call can create an unbounded number of Attendee rows and trigger a calendar update plus an email/ICS to every address, making the endpoint usable for bulk unsolicited invites and resource exhaustion. Bound the array (and reject empty arrays explicitly rather than via the misleading uniqueness error).

MultiEmail imports @calcom/ui from inside the ui package, creating a circular import

This file lives in packages/ui and is exported from packages/ui/index.tsx via MultiEmailLazy, yet it imports Button, EmailField, Icon and Tooltip from "@calcom/ui" (the package's own barrel) instead of relative component paths. That creates a self-referential/circular dependency through the barrel (which also loads the lazy MultiEmail), risking undefined components at runtime and defeating the lazy-loading/bundle-splitting purpose stated in MultiEmailLazy. Import from the relative component modules like other form components in this package do.

No booking status or timing check before adding guests

After only checking the booking exists, the handler creates attendees, updates the calendar event, and sends invite/update emails. It never rejects CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING, or already-ended bookings. The UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings (bookedActions are shown for isBookingInPast && isConfirmed), so guests can be added to meetings that will not happen or have already happened, corrupting attendee lists and generating spurious calendar invites and emails.

Because Prisma OR branches are independent, this SMS cron job can delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows whose retryCount ever exceeds 1, even if they are future/unsent reminders owned by other delivery flows. The retry deletion should be scoped to the same SMS reminders this handler manages.

Missing message or recipient never increments retryCount

If sendTo is missing/empty (for example booking.smsReminderNumber is null) or the rendered message is empty, the handler silently skips the reminder without incrementing retryCount or deleting/scheduling it. Such reminders are fetched again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, so this common invalid-recipient failure mode is not bounded by the new retry limit.

The catch block now performs an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted between findMany and processing (booking cancellation/reschedule cleanup) or because of a transient DB error (P2025/connection error), the exception escapes the per-reminder try/catch, stops processing all remaining unscheduled reminders, and prevents the success response. Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

Caching behavior lost its test coverage

The service still caches authorization and filter conditions (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions at lines 49-50 and the checks at lines 84-94), but this PR deletes the previous "Caching" describe block from the integration tests and adds no replacement. A regression that stops returning the cached Prisma.Sql, rebuilds conditions on every call, or mishandles the cached null filter result would no longer be detected.

Org and team ANY conditions are never executed against the database

The only test that executes SQL through $queryRaw uses scope "user", which produces no array parameter. The org and team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual, so they verify the stored strings/values but not that PostgreSQL and Prisma accept and correctly bind `= ANY(${numberArray})` at runtime. If array serialization or parameter typing fails for ANY, every org/team insights query would fail in production while these tests pass; an executed org or team $queryRaw case is needed.

InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, so `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` now compiles. The runtime schema then rejects it, stores options as null, and all queries silently return the 1=0 condition instead of the caller getting a compile-time error as with the previous discriminated-union options type. This turns a programming error into silently empty insights data.

Single event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR expression

When eventTypeId is the only filter, buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` with no outer parentheses. The previous Prisma WhereInput preserved this OR as a grouped unit in any composition. Now, any caller that composes the public getFilterConditions() result as `... AND ${filter}` gets `( ... AND eventTypeId = ...) OR eventParentId = ...` due to AND/OR precedence, potentially returning bookings matching eventParentId outside the intended preceding conditions. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the standalone filter condition is unsafe and inconsistent with the combined-filter case, which does add parentheses.

Those WorkflowReminder rows stay cancelled=true and their already-scheduled SendGrid emails are still delivered, so a single bad reminder can break cancellation for every other reminder in that cron run.

Reminders cancelled shortly before send time can still be delivered

Cancellation is deferred until scheduledDate is within one hour (scheduledDate <= now+1h) and this cron is described as running every 15 minutes, while the job's first statement deletes EMAIL reminders whose scheduledDate has passed without issuing any SendGrid cancel. A booking cancelled, say, 10 minutes before a reminder's send time can therefore have its next cron run only after SendGrid has already sent the email; the row is then silently deleted by the lte:now deleteMany and the cancellation is lost. There is no check at cancellation time for how soon the reminder fires.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes asynchronously and never awaited

In the allRemainingBookings branch, credentials are iterated with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). The async callbacks suspend at the await, so the main flow continues past this block before any push happens; the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 snapshots apiDeletes without these entries (and the pushed value is the already-awaited result, not a promise). Calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings are thus fire-and-forget: the handler can send cancellation emails and return (or the serverless function can freeze) before the external calendar events are deleted, leaving zombie events, and any rejection is unhandled. Use for...of or Promise.all over map() and push the deleteEvent promises before the Promise.all.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and escapes the try/catch

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) is not awaited, and the surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch rejections from the async callback because forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before the old calendar/video events are actually deleted, and a failing dynamic import or deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. Replace with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) inside the try block.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are still started eagerly for every app

Every value in the appStore object is the result of calling import() when this module is first evaluated, e.g. applecalendar: import("./applecalendar") on line 3 and similarly for all 29 apps. Any module that imports appStore (videoClient, payment helpers, booking handlers, etc.) therefore starts loading every app package even when it only needs one, defeating the purpose of async/lazy loading and paying the import side-effect cost up front. A rejected import for an unused app also becomes an unhandled promise rejection because nothing ever awaits that particular promise. These should be thunks, e.g. applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar"), with callers invoking the thunk so only the requested app is loaded.

requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions before emailing and returning

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) discards the promises returned by the async callbacks. The mutation immediately continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the webhook flow and can return while getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting are still in flight; on serverless runtimes the work may be dropped entirely, leaving the original calendar/video event in place after the booking is marked CANCELLED, and failures are unhandled rejections. Await the deletions, e.g. await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... })), before sending the email.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check uses slot start for both start and end

Both start and end are computed as slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute(); slotEndTime is never used. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before closing) therefore passes the check, so checkIfIsAvailable can approve slots that overrun the host's working hours.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs object identity comparison for empty override never matches

dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The intended special case for an empty override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable all day) is dead code; an early-morning slot on such a day (e.g. 00:00, where slotEnd is not before start and slotStart is not after end) falls through with dateOverrideExist=true and is returned as available.

false_positives.candidate:
No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides, and the timezone test cannot detect a shift

The stated main fix — date overrides of fixed hosts restricting round-robin events — has no test: every scenario added/used here is a single-user event with hosts: []. The added different-timezone assertion at lines 788-804 re-queries with the exact same UTC startTime/endTime window and expects identical UTC slot times, which passes by construction (slots are returned in UTC) and would not catch an override being applied on the wrong local date or shifted across a day boundary in the invitee timezone.

Slots inside a date override skip busy-time checks

When a slot's date matches a date override and the slot is inside the override window, dateOverrideExist is set and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at the end. Consequently a fixed or round-robin host who has a calendar event or an accepted Cal booking during their override hours will still be reported available, allowing double-bookings on override days.

Slots partially overlapping the end of a date override are accepted

A slot is only considered outside the override if its end is at/before the override start or its start is after the override end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 14:00-15:00, 60-minute slot at 14:30) satisfies neither condition, so it is accepted even though half the slot lies outside the host's override availability. The same find()-based logic also stops at the first override for the date, so a slot valid under a second override range on the same day can be rejected because it is outside the first.

Timezone-shifted overrides that cross midnight are placed on the wrong day or dropped

startTime/endTime are derived only from hour()*60+minute() after adding the invitee-organizer offset, discarding any day shift caused by that offset. An override near midnight in the organizer timezone (e.g. 01:00 in UTC+14 viewed by a UTC-10 invitee, shifting to the previous day) is rendered at 01:00-style minutes on the invitee day selected by activeOverrides instead of the shifted day, and if the shifted end passes midnight endTime becomes smaller than startTime so buildSlots discards the range (start >= end). Override slots near midnight will be missing or shown on the wrong date.

Working-hours check rejects split shifts and approves days with no working hours

The code returns unavailable if workingHours.find(...) finds ANY entry for that weekday outside which the slot falls. With split working hours (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) a 13:00 slot is outside the first entry, so it is incorrectly rejected. Conversely, if no entry includes slotStartTime.day(), find returns undefined and the check passes, so a fixed host with no working hours that day is treated as available for a slot generated by another (round-robin) host — defeating the fixed-host enforcement this PR adds.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sender check crashes when integration metadata has no sender

GitHubInstallation unconditionally evaluates integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created before sender was recorded, created through build_integration when state has no sender, or otherwise lacking that nested key will raise KeyError/TypeError here instead of rendering the installation-failed page. OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

Authenticated-user check is bypassed when the Integration row does not yet exist

When Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline state github_authenticated_user to the installer. Because the GitHub webhook that creates the Integration (with sender metadata) is asynchronous and can lag the user's redirect, an attacker who knows/guesses an installation_id and authenticates to GitHub as a different user can complete the pipeline in that window; build_integration only fetches /app/installations/{id}, which contains no sender to validate against, so the PR's mismatch protection is race-dependent and ineffective for fresh/racing installs.

Token exchange and user lookup failures are not converted to the error page

safe_urlopen at line 423 is outside the try/except (only safe_urlread/parse_qsl is guarded), and get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) at line 434 is also unguarded. test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path

The updated test_installation_not_found drives the setup endpoint with state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which fails OAuthLoginView's pipeline-signature check and renders 'Invalid installation request.' before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever calls get_installation_info.
